body.notes: Checked every step of the H23 proof in properties.md against the recorded statement. (1) Lemma J: strict concavity of z^r on [0, inf) for 0<r<1 gives E[Z^r] <= (E Z)^r with equality iff Z is constant a.s.; correct. (2) Applied with Z = D^2, r = 1/4: Z >= 0, E[Z] = sigma^2 finite, Z^(1/4) = |D|^0.5, so nu <= sigma^0.5; correct. (3) D^2 constant a.s. iff |D| constant a.s.; correct. Both directions of 'exactly when' follow from the iff in Lemma J; verified the converse directly: |D| = c a.s. with c > 0 gives nu = c^0.5 = sigma^0.5. (4) sigma > 0 implies P(D != 0) > 0, so nu = E|D|^0.5 > 0, hence H > 0; correct. Finite variance gives the finite mean the notation needs. Numeric check: 20000 random weighted discrete laws (2-7 points, scales 1e-3 to 1e3) all gave H in (0, 1); symmetric two-point law gives H = 1; two-point law with weights 0.3/0.7 (|D| not constant) gives 0.937. Nothing wrong or missing.

Checked every step of the H24 proof in properties.md against the recorded statement. (1) h_U = 2*3^-0.75 = 0.87738 lies in (0,1), so log h_U < 0 and p = log 0.5 / log h_U = 5.29880 > 0; correct. (2) For p > 0, u -> 2u^p - 1 is continuous and strictly increasing on [0,1], sending 0 to -1 and 1 to 1; correct. (3) h_U^p = exp(log 0.5) = 0.5, so h_U maps to 0; verified to 30 digits. (4) By H23 (which I checked separately and confirmed) H is in (0,1]; strict monotonicity gives E > -1 and E <= 1, and E < 0 iff H < h_U; correct. (5) H10 re-derived: for the uniform law on (b,c), a = (c-b)/2, nu = (2/3)a^0.5, sigma^2 = a^2/3, H = (2/3)*3^0.25 = 2*3^-0.75 = h_U, so E = 0; confirmed by quadrature for three intervals (differences below 1e-24). Nothing wrong. One remark on wording, not an error: 'the uniform distribution' means the continuous uniform law on an interval, as in H10; a discrete uniform law has a different H.
